subject: POC Trial Planning: workload intake & success criteria - AcmeHealth
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery — next steps & POC planning

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Summary of what you’re trying to evaluate:
- Surface-level triage + summarization for clinical intake forms (backend call volume, low-latency requirement)
- Maintain PII controls (no retention outside dedicated environment)
- Validate cost/latency tradeoffs across peak windows

Suggested POC scope (proposed):
- 4-week trial in Redwood Dedicated (isolated pool)
- Integration: ingest request/response via our API + optional sidecar for request replay
- Success criteria (please confirm):
  * Functional: extraction + summarization accuracy >= 88% on your evaluation set
  * Performance: p95 inference latency < 350ms for single-request flow under target concurrency 
  * Cost: average token cost per session within your target budget (TBD)

Workload intake — what we need from you (attached template):
- Typical steady-state RPS: 
- Peak burst RPS and expected burst duration: 
- Average request token length and average response token length: 
- Concurrency targets (warm and steady) and expected traffic patterns (e.g., 9am-11am spikes, weekend-low)
- A 10-20 minute sample request logfile or CSV / replayable sample (anonymized)

Ownership & timeline (proposed):
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) / Ben (SE) / Dylan (Infra ops) — onboarding + trial instrumentation
- AcmeHealth: Alex (Product), Priya (Engineering), SaaSInfra (platform owner) — provide workload samples, sign-off on criteria
- Next steps: please complete the attached workload_profile_template.xlsx and return by Tue 2027-03-30 so we can scope infra and lock schedule. I’ve attached a draft POC_success_criteria.docx and a short checklist for the trial.

I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff for the week of 3/31 once we have the workload profile. Any questions, call me directly at (415) 555-0123.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: workload_profile_template.xlsx, POC_success_criteria.docx

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya@acmehealth.com>, SaaSInfra <saasinfra@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery — next steps & POC planning

Thanks Marissa — great summary. We’re aligned on scope. See initial workload answers below (we’ll fill the template and send sample logs by EOD Monday):

Workload snapshot (initial):
- Typical steady-state RPS: 5 requests/sec
- Peak burst RPS: ~25 requests/sec for bursts lasting ~3-8 minutes (usually correlated with clinic check-ins)
- Average request token length: ~150 tokens (form text + metadata)
- Average response token length: ~110 tokens (summaries + extracted fields)
- Concurrency targets: 10 concurrent sessions typical; allow for 30 concurrent during sustained peak windows
- Burst pattern: daily spikes at 08:30-09:30 and smaller peaks 13:00-14:00 PST; weekdays only

Timeline preferences:
- Integration window: 2 weeks to instrument and replay sample traffic
- Trial duration: 4 weeks of monitored traffic with weekly checkpoints

Questions / asks from our side:
- Can you confirm p95 lat <350ms at our median payloads under 10 concurrency?
- Any recommended model/config (half-precision vs int8) for cost/latency balance?
- Also need a brief note about data handling — we require no model retention and audit logging for inference calls

We’ll upload anonymized sample logs and the completed template by 2027-03-30. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Alex
Alex Johnson | Product Lead, AcmeHealth
alex.johnson@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T13:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / discovery — next steps & POC planning

Hi all — quick technical notes based on the initial workload you provided:

1) Performance & model guidance:
- For 150-token requests / 110-token responses the token counts are moderate; we typically recommend a quantized 8-bit variant of a 13B model for a good latency/cost balance on Dedicated pools.
- Expectation: with a dedicated 1-2 GPU pool and batching tuned to 20-50ms windows we can hit p95 ~250-350ms at 10 concurrency. If you need consistent <200ms p95 we’ll need a higher-perf GPU or model slicing.

2) Concurrency & bursts:
- For short bursts to 25 RPS we’ll rely on autoscale + burst capacity; please confirm acceptable warm-start time for scale (we assume ~60-90s cold scale)
- Recommend enabling KV cache/prefix cache if request patterns reuse context per session (saves tokens and latency)

3) Testing & data requirements:
- Please provide a 10-20 minute anonymized replay and a small labeled eval set (50-100 examples) so we can validate extraction accuracy.
- Format: newline-delimited JSONL or CSV; sample anonymization checklist attached.

4) Success metrics to instrument:
- Functional: precision/recall on extraction; qualitative summary score (1-5) from clinicians
- Performance: p50/p95 latency, error rate, throughput (RPS sustained), cold-start latency
- Cost: estimated $/1000 tokens for the chosen configuration

I’ve attached a short redwood_poc_checklist.pdf that covers the infra pieces we’ll need for the trial. Happy to join the kickoff to run through the checklist and instrumenting metrics.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_poc_checklist.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

If that schedule works I’ll send the invite and attach Ben’s checklist + our trial playbook to the calendar. Looking forward to getting started.

Cheers,
Marissa
